title: Chile Colorado
origin: Uploaded as YouTube link (https://youtu.be/Ws7vLUbxhXQ); quantities from the linked printable recipe

steps.action: Boil in a stockpot until the chiles are soft, about 20 min:
items: 8 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
3 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
1 dried chile de árbol, stemmed and seeded

steps.action: Meanwhile, trim excess fat and cut into even bite-sized pieces:
items: 3 lb stew meat (chuck roast, wild game, etc.)

steps.action: Mix in a bowl; toss the meat to coat generously:
items: 2 Tbsp Kent's Original Seasoning (or salt, pepper, and garlic powder to taste)

steps.action: Brown on all sides in a large cast iron skillet over medium-high, in 2 batches, about 5 min per batch; move to a Dutch oven and scrape in the drippings:
items: 6 Tbsp cooking oil (avocado, olive, etc.), 2 to 3 Tbsp per batch
Floured meat, shaken free of excess flour

steps.action: Strain the chiles, reserving the water. Blend until smooth:
Stir into the meat; cover and simmer until tender, 1½ to 2 hr. Thin with more chile water if desired:

steps.text: Remove the bay leaves before serving.

edits: Chile boil time: blog/video say about 15 min, recipe card says about 20 min; card used
Cumin form not specified; ground assumed
Seasoning the sauce to taste is from the blog text; the recipe card seasons only the flour
Scraping the skillet drippings in is from the blog; the card omits it
Leftover chile water freezes well for future stews and soups; the red sauce also works as enchilada sauce (source tips)
